title: Nvidia GPU prices spike in Japan; prices up to 41% higher than Amazon US — RTX 5060 Ti sees the biggest increase among the RTX 50-series stack
key_facts: A Reddit user (u/Chaise91) posted a photo of Japanese retail prices for Nvidia RTX 50-series cards.
Prices ran 5.66% to 41.1% above Amazon US listings.
Tom's Hardware's table found average gaps from 12.71% (RTX 5080) to 41.10% (RTX 5060 Ti 8GB), before tax.
With an 8.5% US tax rate the gap is 3.88% to 30.04%.
Reports say Nvidia may halt RTX 5090 production in favour of AI data-centre GPUs.
The outlet hopes it is a local fluke but warns US prices could follow.
quote_evidence: According to u/Chaise91’s post on the r/pcmasterrace subreddit, retail prices for some of the best gaming GPUs are somewhere between 5.66% and 41.1% higher compared to Amazon U.S. listings.
While this may be bad news for Japanese gamers, it could also serve as a harbinger for the United States, as these pricing trends tend to travel westward.
why_it_matters_hint: Gaming graphics cards are getting dearer as memory and AI demand squeeze supply.
notes: Single Reddit photo plus Tom's Hardware comparison; date of the photo not given.
